en: Morning dew on a banana leaf is water vapor from the air that condensed into a liquid upon touching the cool plant surface.
Seawater in Manila Bay is a homogeneous mixture where solid salt crystals are completely dissolved in liquid water.
The reddish-brown rust on corrugated iron roofs forms when iron chemically reacts with oxygen and moisture in the humid air.
Solid coconut oil turning into clear liquid coconut oil when heated in a pan is a reversible physical change.
Pumice stones from Philippine volcanoes float on water because their porous structure traps air, making them less dense than liquid water.
Muddy water from the Pasig River after heavy rain is a heterogeneous mixture containing visible suspended solid soil particles.
Mothballs placed inside wooden cabinets slowly shrink over time because the solid naphthalene directly sublimates into a gas.
Burning dried rice husks to ash produces a chemical change because the original solid material cannot be recovered.
Black sand on Camiguin beaches contains magnetic iron particles that can be separated from non-magnetic silica using a magnet.
Sun-drying bangus on bamboo racks causes the liquid water inside the fish to evaporate into water vapor.
Freshly squeezed coconut milk is a mixture where tiny droplets of liquid fat are evenly suspended throughout liquid water.
Stirring solid sugar into a glass of cold calamansi juice demonstrates solubility as the sugar crystals dissolve completely.
